items.title: Task 1 tests the fake seam, not the real runCLI fallback
items.detail: Task 1’s cross-package test drives fakeReviewer.Review, which newly calls resolveTimeout itself. It can pass even if runCLI—the production path named by A1—does not call resolveTimeout or applies a different unset-timeout fallback. The grep checks only that resolveTimeout exists. Add verification that exercises or otherwise directly pins runCLI’s use of the shared resolver; otherwise G1’s no-drift evidence is indirect and defeatable.

items.title: Task 1 disagrees about the explicit-timeout cancellation row
items.detail: The plan.md Task 1 section requires a second row with a short explicit Timeout and longer fake sleep, but plan.index.json Task 1 specifies only the unset-timeout fallback test and its verify selector does not clearly require the cancellation row. Either include the row explicitly in the executable task or remove it from plan.md.

items.title: Boundary tests weaken a representable strict-containment case
items.detail: Task 2 classifies MaxDuration-SessionMargin and MaxDuration-Grace as saturation points where only non-strict bounds are asserted. At exactly those inputs, adding the margin produces representable MaxDuration and is still strictly greater than the input. Assert the strict relation at equality, reserving the non-strict-only rule for inputs above the threshold.

items.title: Prompt invariant "never push except push_pr" is now false: archived pr cleanup pushes too
items.detail: This wave's archive.go change (prCleanup, archive.go:179-198) makes an `archived` stop's `cleanup` list carry a literal `git push origin <branch>` / `git push -u origin <branch>` command for the pr disposition — a second place a takt op instructs a push, not covered by this line's sole named exception `(push_pr)`. The op-table's `stop` bullet (commands/takt.md:33) already generically tells the agent to run confirmed cleanup commands, so this line now contradicts it inside the same file: an LLM strictly honouring the Invariants section's 'never push except push_pr' could refuse the very cleanup push task 7 exists to hand back. The identical stale sentence is duplicated in hosts/copilot/skills/takt/SKILL.md:46 (same text, not part of the crossHostInvariants test set, so it won't be caught by TestPromptInvariantsReadTheSameOnEveryHost either). Neither file is mentioned anywhere in this run's own docs/takt/lets-work-on-60-and-62/plan.md task 8, which only targets README.md and the design spec — so this gap is not already tracked to be fixed by a later task in this run.

items.title: recordReviewDeadline's failure path is never exercised
items.detail: The new block `if p := f.getenv("TAKT_FAKE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_FILE"); p != "" { if err := recordReviewDeadline(ctx, p); err != nil { return errorResult(...) } }` (fake.go:45-49) has no test that makes the write fail (e.g. a path in a nonexistent directory), so the errorResult branch this new code adds is untested. TestBackendFallbackMatchesTheShippedDefault only exercises the success path via a valid t.TempDir() file.

items.title: Added assertion re-invokes commitBundle rather than checking preparePushPR's own call
items.detail: Lines 188-191 call `commitBundle(context.Background(), r.ws, r.bdir, r.slug, "pr body")` a second, separate time to assert `committed==false`. Since `r.ws` is the same zero-value workspace (Dir.InRepo false) that preparePushPR's own internal commitBundle call at line 171 already ran through without error, this second call is a fresh, independent invocation rather than an observation of what preparePushPR actually did — it documents commitBundle's no-op behaviour in isolation more than it verifies the integration point, though it does satisfy the brief's explicit request for 'one assertion making that explicit'.

items.title: preparePushPR's new commitBundle error path is untested
items.detail: The new `if _, _, err = commitBundle(ctx, r.ws, r.bdir, r.slug, "pr body"); err != nil { return err }` propagates a commit failure exactly like the pre-existing read/write failures preparePushPR already returns, but no test forces commitBundle to fail here (e.g. a broken repo/lock) to confirm the error surfaces through preparePushPR and ultimately fails `run` the same way assertPreparePushPRRefuses covers for the spec/goals reads. The codebase already has a pattern for simulating git-commit failures (internal/cli/archive_test.go's TestArchiveCommitIsRetriedAfterASoftReset) that could have been reused here.

items.title: Cleanup-empty checkpoints skip op/reason assertions
items.detail: In TestArchivedPROffersThePushUntilItIsDone (also at line 710), the checks `len(got) != 0` / `len(again) != 0` read `o["cleanup"]` without first asserting `o["op"] == "stop"` and `o["reason"] == stopArchived` (as the earlier and later checkpoints in the same test do, e.g. lines 673-674, 683-684, 722-723). cleanupOf silently returns an empty slice when the "cleanup" key is absent or of the wrong shape, so if `next` regressed to returning a different op entirely at these points, the 'nothing offered' assertions would pass anyway, masking the regression in exactly the rows this test exists to pin (G7's zero-cleanup cases).
